money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency is the Boliviano (BOB). Declare all amounts more than $US10,000 on arrival. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. US dollars are the most easily exchangeable foreign currency. ATMs are available in cities throughout Bolivia. Many businesses accept international credit cards.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They include long prison sentences in local jails. Prison conditions are poor.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: You must always carry photo identification in Bolivia. This should be a photocopy of your passport bio page and the Bolivian entry stamp pages.
laws.heading: Proof of identity

laws.rule: It's illegal to remove national treasures, including: pre-Columbian artefacts certain historical paintings items of Spanish colonial architecture and history some native textiles certain flora, fauna and fossils It's illegal to excavate or collect fossils without written approval.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships are legal, but they aren't widely accepted.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ travellers

laws.rule: Not all medication available over the counter or by prescription in Australia is available in other countries. Some may even be considered illegal or a controlled substance, even if prescribed by an Australian doctor. If you plan to bring medication, check if it's legal in Bolivia. Take enough legal medicine for your trip. what the medication is that it's for personal use
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: To drive in Bolivia, you need both: a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver’s licences may not be accepted) an International Driving Permit (IDP) Get your IDP before you leave.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Travellers entering or leaving Bolivia declare cash on the customs Form 250 once they carry US$10,000 or more. Bolivian customs pages differ on the ceiling: one news notice says up to US$20,000 either way, and the traveller-regime page says up to US$50,000 on entry and US$20,000 on exit; larger amounts must move through regulated financial institutions. Check the current figure with Aduana Nacional before travel. US$10,000 is about A$14,200 (RBA 30 Oct 2026: A$1 = USD 0.7040).
laws.penalty_signal: 30% of the undeclared foreign currency is retained; for an inaccurate declaration, 30% of the difference between what was found and what was declared

laws.rule: Traveller allowance: up to 3 litres of alcoholic drinks, 400 cigarettes, and 50 cigars or 500 grams of cut tobacco.
Medicines for personal use are allowed with an express medical prescription, in a quantity not above three units (boxes or bottles).

layers.process: Filming and photography for commercial, cultural, educational or scientific purposes in any national protected area run by SERNAP (this covers Madidi, Sajama and Toro Toro) needs a written request and approval from SERNAP's Executive Director, under Resolución Administrativa 048/2017 (18 August 2017). Charges are set in US dollars, payable in bolivianos: profit-making still images US$100 a day for national firms and US$300 for foreign firms (about A$142 and A$426); profit-making filming US$200 and US$600 a day (about A$284 and A$852); feature films, shorts and documentaries for profit US$600 and US$1,500 a day (about A$852 and A$2,131); scientific research filming US$200 per area for foreigners and US$50 for nationals (about A$284 and A$71). Rate: RBA, 30 October 2026, A$1 = US$0.7040. The rule is aimed at commercial, cultural, educational and scientific work; it doesn't read as a rule for a visitor's own photos. Tourist entry fees for individual parks were not found on an official page.

sources.title: Reglamento de filmaciones y tomas fotográficas (RA 048/2017)
